newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU improves odds on BT-MCI merger clearance.
newsitem.headline: EU improves odds on BT-MCI merger clearance.

text.p: European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said Thursday that he was happy with the state of the British telecommunications market, improving the odds that the EU will approve British Telecom Plc's $20 billion acquisition of MCI Communications Corp.
Although BT still had a "de facto' dominant position in the British market, Van Miert said, "They are not misusing their dominant position. Competitors are given a chance in the British market."

BT and Washington-based MCI, the second-biggest telecommunications company in the United States, announced this week that they were pooling their operations in their Concert joint venture, creating a multinational giant with a market value of $54 billion, roughly the same as AT&T Corp.

However, the merger, the largest cross-border deal of its kind, faces its most important anti-trust test in the United States, where legislation forbids a foreign company from taking more than 20 percent in an American firm unless its home market is effectively open to competition.
BT already has a 20 percent stake in MCI, which it acquired in 1993 when the two companies launched Concert to provide telecommunication services to multinational companies.
That transaction was cleared by both U.S. and EU authorities after several provisions were introduced to avoid, in particular, BT controlling or influencing MCI.
"It was an easy case because both markets were already liberalised," Van Miert told a conference on competition policy organised by a Brussels-based weekly newspaper.
This contrasted with the more recent global telecommunication alliances that the European Commission, the EU's executive body, had to deal with, Van Miert said.

He singled out the Global One deal among France Telecom, Deutsche Telekom and Sprint Corp., which took almost two years to clear due to strong resistance from the French and German governments to allow competition in their domestic markets.
Van Miert declined to comment on whether the full merger of BT and MCI will be as easy a case now as in 1993.
The commission was still assessing whether it will fall under the bloc's "fast-track" merger rules, which allow for clearance within a month of formal notification if no serious problems arise.

To qualify for a review under the regulation, the two companies must each have a European turnover of 250 million European currency units ($317.3 million). BT met this threshold, Van Miert said, but MCI's figure was being checked.
BT's head of EU affairs said Monday he was confident the deal would be cleared under the merger rules.
